title: Review of Step Count Accuracy in Samsung Health App
body:
Overall, Samsung Health is a very good app with many useful features. However, I have concerns about the accuracy of the step count rankings. Some users appear to record over 120,000 steps in a single day on a regular basis, which seems highly unrealistic.

These figures raise questions about the accuracy and fairness of the rankings. They can also be discouraging for people who are genuinely trying to stay active and improve their fitness, as it becomes difficult to compete with what appear to be inaccurate or inflated step counts.

I would encourage Samsung to review how steps are tracked and validated to ensure the leaderboard reflects genuine activity. This would help maintain user trust and provide fair motivation for everyone using the app.

title: Never syncs properly
body:
I’ve had a galaxy watch active for about half a year now and I love the watch, but the app drives me up the wall. It never syncs and loses data. I have months on the app where it just says “no data recorded”. Yesterday I did 8000 steps according to my watch but every single time I synced the app it said I did just over 7000. I should be able to just open the app and have it connected but I have to jump through many hoops every time to just get it to connect to my watch, and even then it doesn’t sync properly.
I’ve done every troubleshooting suggestion in the reply’s from Samsung: everything is updated, automatic sync is on, background refresh is on and I open the watch app and let it connect before trying but it still doesn’t sync properly.
If you have a health app it should at the bare minimum sync the steps properly! It’s a health tracker!!
It’s really disappointing and frustrating because I love the watch but I would not recommend it to anyone for the sole reason of this app.
Needs to be fixed soon.

Samsung is rubbish for Fitness 
It’s just a watch you play with 
If you want fitness data running cycling swimming Samsung watch ain’t it 
Really disappointing

Update ditch this app if you have a Samsung galaxy watch and if your into cycling and download Strava app iPhone and strava from Samsung to install it on the watch. Strava watch app has an automatic pause and after a ride you just hit sync on the watch and it will load straight to the app it also stores the rides as well on the watch 
Gives a map of route, distance stats speed on a graph heart rate graph and elevation graph and effort through ride 
Also has live tracking with other cyclist in the premium option 
If you have a garmin on your bike as well it allows you to sync garmin to strava 
And migrate rides from strava to garmin 
also does the same for outdoor and indoor  running, Nordic skiing outdoor and indoor cycling hiking or just a workout heart rate

None of the data syncs with Apple health unless you use a 3rd party app which only syncs individual runs/activities. Overall works ok though. A few sync issues but usually only when restarting the iPhone. Simply toggle your Bluetooth on and off and all is well again.

title: It kind of does what it needs to do
body:
The user experience is not great. No auto-sync meaning that every time you open the app, the data is out of date and you need to pull down to refresh. That usually does not sync anything so you need to try again a few more times. Than finally you get your data into the app. Now you need to reload Together tab. Now that Together tab is reloaded, you need to go back to main tab to resync with your watch so that the info on your watch is up to date. Oh yeah and also if you do not do this several-minute-process every die, you will likely lose data from your watch. It will be on your watch but the app will be like “meh too old, I am not going to sync that”. Also, it is not possible to share your sleep or steps from your watch with any other applications. 

So overall, it is not like it does not work. It does when you are patient enough and remember to go through the process daily. I am glad that they at least brought the Together feature to iPhone users and that they are still improving the app. However, at the moment the user experience makes me want to hit myself with a chair out of frustration.

title: Love the hardware, hate the iOS software
body:
I absolutely love my Samsung Gear S2 Classic. I love it so much that it is the only watch I wear now. It has replaced a Bulova as my casual watch, and a Rotary as my work watch (I have different straps for it). It is the perfect size (unlike most smart watches) and the battery lasts a week. I love it so much I may buy a second one for when it gets discontinued!

Unfortunately, I can’t say the same for the iOS app. The original app that came bundled within Samsung Gear S was totally useless, so I was quite happy when this update came out. But guess what? It doesn’t work with my watch! The crappy old one does, the better new one doesn’t. How does it even make sense to release an app that does not work with probably the best smart watch hardware (pound for pound) that Samsung has released? Beats me...
